o: We need the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray that reads the same forwards and backwards. Every single element is a palindrome, so the answer is at least max(nums). In Example 2 the maximal palindrome centered at value 3 is [1,2,3,2,1] with sum 9; in Example 5 the whole array is one element. The key constraint observation: **all nums[i] are positive** (1 <= nums[i]). Therefore, for a fixed center, extending a palindrome never decreases its sum — the best palindromic subarray at each center is simply its *maximal* extension. So we only need, for every possible center, the largest palindrome around it, which is exactly what Manacher's algorithm computes in linear time.
k: All values are positive, so the best palindrome at a given center is its maximal expansion — no need to consider shorter ones.
Manacher's algorithm finds the maximal palindrome radius at every center (both odd and even length) in O(n).
Prefix sums turn 'sum of subarray' into a subtraction once endpoints are known.

a.i: For each index (and each adjacent pair), expand outward while the characters match, tracking the widest palindrome found. With positive numbers the widest palindrome at a center has the maximum sum there, so we can stop expanding at the first mismatch. Worst case (all elements equal) is quadratic, but it is simple and passes moderate inputs.
s: Build prefix sums so any subarray sum is O(1).
For each odd center i, expand l=i, r=i while nums[l-1]==nums[r+1]; update answer with pre[r+1]-pre[l].
Do the same for even centers (l=i, r=i+1) when nums[i]==nums[i+1].
a.t: O(n^2) worst case (e.g., all-equal arrays force full expansions), typically much faster; prefix sums make each evaluation O(1).

a.i: Manacher's algorithm reuses previously computed palindrome radii to compute, in amortized O(1) per position, d1[i] (radius of the longest odd palindrome centered at i) and d2[i] (radius of the longest even palindrome whose left half starts at i). Combined with prefix sums, the best candidate through an odd center i spans [i-d1[i]+1, i+d1[i]] and through an even center spans [i-d2[i], i+d2[i]-1]. Because values are positive these maximal palindromes dominate all shorter ones at the same center.
s: Compute d1[] and d2[] with the standard Manacher two-pointer technique.
Answer candidates: pre[i+d1[i]] - pre[i-d1[i]+1] for odd, pre[i+d2[i]] - pre[i-d2[i]] for even.
a.t: O(n) — Manacher processes each position with amortized constant work; prefix sums are linear.
a.sp: O(n) for the radii arrays and prefix sums.

w: Lead with the observation that all values are positive — it collapses 'max sum over many palindromic lengths' into 'sum of the maximal palindrome per center'. In an interview, present expand-around-center first, then upgrade to Manacher for the strict O(n) bound. Pitfalls: forgetting even-length palindromes, off-by-one errors in Manacher's mirror indices, and integer overflow of sums in C++/Java (use 64-bit). Follow-ups: what if negative numbers were allowed (then you'd need max-subarray queries over expanding ranges, e.g., sparse tables on prefix sums per center); counting rather than maximizing.
